paper.core_task: Evaluating motion utilization in language-guided video segmentation via motion-centric probing.

contributions.name: A motion-centric probing and evaluation technique for video MLLMs
contributions.author_claim_text: we provide a study of the ability of video MLLMs in utilizing motion information within language-guided video segmentation. Towards the latter, we create a motion-centric probing and evaluation technique
contributions.description: The authors propose a method to assess how video multimodal large language models utilize motion by creating a probing technique that pairs a static keyframe with the original video to mislead models.

contributions.name: A new motion-centric benchmark for video referring segmentation
contributions.author_claim_text: We propose a novel benchmark that is motion-centric through the use of a static keyframe paired with the dynamic video to mislead the referring segmentation methods
contributions.description: A new evaluation benchmark is introduced that uses a static keyframe combined with the dynamic video to test if models can distinguish real motion from static visual cues.

contributions.name: Strong static-biased baselines for referring video segmentation
contributions.author_claim_text: we establish strong single-image and semi-temporal baselines for referring video segmentation using powerful multi-modal large language models
contributions.description: The authors create strong baselines that are intentionally biased towards static information, using models like Qwen2.5-VL and SAM 2.0, which outperform existing state-of-the-art methods.

novelty_claims.text: It introduces a novel motion-centric probing technique to study the capabilities of video MLLMs in utilizing motion information within language-guided video segmentation tasks.
